title: Indonesian Knowledge
description: Get to know Indonesia: geography, a short history, its diversity, and everyday public etiquette.

stations.title: Geography & Nature
stations.summary: Why Indonesia is fertile, earthquake-prone, and spans three time zones at once — it is all about position.
points: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago, with more than 17,000 islands.
The five largest islands: Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Papua.
Straddled by the equator → a tropical climate with two seasons: dry and rainy.
On the Pacific Ring of Fire → many volcanoes, fertile soil, but also earthquake risk.

questions.prompt: How many time zones does Indonesia have?
When it is 12:00 in Jakarta (WIB), the time in Papua (WIT) is...
questions.explain: WIT is UTC+9, two hours ahead of WIB at UTC+7.

questions.prompt: Being on the Pacific Ring of Fire means Indonesia has...
options: Many volcanoes & earthquake risk, but fertile soils
questions.explain: Tectonic plate boundaries create volcanoes and quakes, and volcanic soils are very fertile.

stations.title: A Short History
stations.summary: A handful of dates shaped modern Indonesia — the ones that come up most in daily life.
points: 17 August 1945: the Proclamation of Independence read by Sukarno–Hatta in Jakarta.
28 October 1928: the Youth Pledge — one homeland, one nation, one language: Indonesian.
The national flag is the red-and-white Merah Putih. The anthem Indonesia Raya was composed by W. R. Supratman.
Independence Day is marked every 17 August with flag ceremonies across the country.

questions.explain: 17 August is celebrated as the country's Independence Day.

questions.prompt: The Youth Pledge (28 October 1928) declared one unifying language, namely...
questions.explain: The pledge united the archipelago around one homeland, one nation, and Indonesian as the language of unity.

questions.prompt: Who composed the national anthem Indonesia Raya?
questions.explain: Wage Rudolf Supratman introduced Indonesia Raya at the Second Youth Congress in 1928.

cards.back: Youth Pledge: one homeland, nation, language

stations.title: Unity in Diversity
stations.summary: Hundreds of ethnic groups, languages, and faiths are daily reality here — not something to fear.
points: The national motto is Bhinneka Tunggal Ika — unity in diversity, literally 'different, yet still one'.
It comes from the Sutasoma text written by Mpu Tantular in the Majapahit era.
Pancasila is the state philosophy with five principles; the first is belief in the One Supreme God.
There are hundreds of ethnic groups and more than 700 local languages; Indonesian bridges them all.

options: United we stand, divided we fall
One nation, one language, one state
questions.explain: The phrase from the Sutasoma text describes an archipelago that stays united through all its differences.

questions.prompt: How many principles does Pancasila have?
questions.explain: Pancasila has five principles, from belief in the One Supreme God to social justice for all Indonesians.

questions.prompt: An everyday example of gotong royong (communal cooperation) is...
options: Neighbours cleaning the drainage ditch together
Waiting for the workers without lifting a finger
questions.explain: Gotong royong means working together for the common good — a signature of Indonesian community life.

cards.back: Unity in diversity (from the Sutasoma text)

stations.title: Public Etiquette
stations.summary: Public space belongs to everyone. Small courtesies make it comfortable for all.
points: Queueing is the simplest form of fairness: first come, first served.
Put rubbish in a bin; carry it home if there is no bin around.
Follow traffic rules: wear a helmet, buckle up, and obey signs and traffic lights.
Respect differences: no insults, no hate speech, and keep your voice down in shared spaces.

questions.prompt: At a busy counter, the right behaviour is to...
options: Cut in because you are in a hurry
Ask someone else to queue for you
questions.explain: Queueing keeps things fair for everyone, especially those who arrived earlier.

questions.prompt: The small habit that most helps keep shared spaces clean is...
options: Binning rubbish and separating what can be recycled
Piling rubbish in front of the house
questions.explain: Unmanaged waste pollutes the environment; sorting makes recycling possible.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows proper road conduct?
options: Wearing a helmet and stopping at red lights
Overtaking on the left without looking
Riding against traffic to arrive faster
questions.explain: Helmets and seat belts save lives; signs and lights keep everyone moving safely.

cards.back: Helmet · seat belt · obey signs & lights
